## A shared preamble

`preamble` puts Typst code ahead of every block, so a document defines its helpers once.
It takes code, a path to a `.typ` file, or a list of either:

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-render:
    preamble: "_typst/preamble.typ"
```

The file beside this page defines one `badge` function:

```typ
#let badge(body, fill: teal) = box(
  fill: fill.lighten(70%),
  radius: 4pt,
  inset: (x: 8pt, y: 5pt),
  text(size: 11pt, body),
)
```

Every block can then call it:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| preamble: "_typst/preamble.typ"
#stack(dir: ltr, spacing: 6pt, badge[svg], badge(fill: orange)[png], badge(fill: purple)[pdf])
```
````

```{typst}
//| preamble: "_typst/preamble.typ"
#stack(dir: ltr, spacing: 6pt, badge[svg], badge(fill: orange)[png], badge(fill: purple)[pdf])
```

A path is resolved against the document directory, and a leading `/` means the project root.
Short code is written straight into the option instead:

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-render:
    preamble: "#set text(font: \"Inter\", size: 12pt)"
```

## An external file

`file` compiles a `.typ` file in place of the body of the block, so a figure kept beside the document needs no copy in the text:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| file: "_typst/diagram.typ"
```
````

```{typst}
//| file: "_typst/diagram.typ"
```

The body of such a block is ignored.
Every other option still applies, so the file can be labelled, captioned, and aligned like any block.

## Multi-page output

A block that produces several pages is included page by page.
`pages` selects them, and `layout-ncol` arranges them side by side:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| width: 5cm
//| height: 3cm
//| pages: all
//| layout-ncol: "3"
#align(center + horizon)[Page 1]
#pagebreak()
#align(center + horizon)[Page 2]
#pagebreak()
#align(center + horizon)[Page 3]
```
````

```{typst}
//| width: 5cm
//| height: 3cm
//| pages: all
//| layout-ncol: "3"
#align(center + horizon)[Page 1]
#pagebreak()
#align(center + horizon)[Page 2]
#pagebreak()
#align(center + horizon)[Page 3]
```

`pages` accepts `all`, one number, a range such as `1-3`, a set such as `2,5`, and an open range such as `3-`.
Without `layout-ncol` the pages are stacked vertically.

## Input variables

`input` passes key-value pairs to the Typst compiler, which reads them through `sys.inputs`.
On a block the pairs are comma-separated:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| input: "label=beta,fill=purple"
#let name = sys.inputs.at("label", default: "none")
#let fill = sys.inputs.at("fill", default: "gray")
#box(fill: eval(fill + ".lighten(70%)"), radius: 4pt, inset: 8pt)[Built for #name]
```
````

```{typst}
//| input: "label=beta,fill=purple"
#let name = sys.inputs.at("label", default: "none")
#let fill = sys.inputs.at("fill", default: "gray")
#box(fill: eval(fill + ".lighten(70%)"), radius: 4pt, inset: 8pt)[Built for #name]
```

Globally it is a map, and every block of the document reads the same pairs:

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-render:
    input:
      label: beta
      fill: purple
```

Use `.at(name, default: ...)`, because a missing input stops the compilation.

## Where the images land

Compiled images are written under `./assets/typst-render`, relative to the document, in a subdirectory named after it.
The figures on this page sit in `examples/assets/typst-render/output-and-files/`.

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-render:
    output-directory: "./assets/typst-render"
    output-source: false
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `output-directory` | Where images are written. An empty string writes none, which leaves them in the render cache, where a deployed site cannot reach them. |
| `output-filename` | Names the image for one block. A leading `/` means the project root; anything else is resolved against `output-directory`. |
| `output-source` | Writes the compiled Typst source beside each image, with the same stem and a `.typ` extension. |

: The three options that decide what reaches the disk. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

Without `output-filename`, the name comes from the label of the block, or from its position in the document.

## The cache

Compiled images are cached between renders, keyed by the source and the options that shape it.
A block that has not changed is not compiled again:

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-render:
    cache: true
    cache-refresh: false
```

Set `cache: false` on a block that reads something the cache key cannot see, such as a file the preamble loads.
Set `cache-refresh: true` to remove stale files of the current output format after each render.

## Native Typst output

`output: asis` passes the code through to the Typst writer instead of compiling an image, so Typst output receives real Typst:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| output: asis
#circle(radius: 1cm, fill: blue)
```
````

Every other writer compiles an image, as usual.
With `output: asis` the `width` and `height` options are ignored, and `margin` becomes the inset of the block.
